title: Power Automate: Delinea Secret Server as a credential provider for desktop flows
summary: Hold: the cost rating and its rationale say only staff time is a known cost, despite the briefing documenting applicable desktop-flow run charges. The roadmap facts, existing credential controls and security-update details are supported; the new Delinea provider's setup and specific requirements remain undocumented.

claims.claim: Existing CyberArk credentials retrieve CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault at runtime.
claims.quote: This feature enables you to create a Power Automate credential that retrieves CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault during runtime.

claims.claim: Azure Key Vault credentials used in desktop-flow connections sign into the machine at runtime in attended and unattended runs.
claims.quote: Used in a desktop flow connection, the credential is used to sign into the machine during runtime (attended and unattended runs).

claims.claim: The existing credential guides say Get credential produces a sensitive variable.
claims.quote: Define the name of your produced variable. This variable is marked as sensitive and can't be modified.

claims.claim: The CyberArk and Azure Key Vault guides describe the sensitive credential variable's value as not stored in logs.
claims.quote: This variable is marked as "sensitive" and can't be changed. This means the value of this variable isn't stored in the logs.

claims.claim: Unpatched versions 2.62 through 2.66 can expose global sensitive variables used in local subflows.
claims.quote: A potential vulnerability ... that can expose sensitive values in flow execution logs affects Power Automate for desktop versions 2.62 through 2.66. ... The issue affects only flows that use global sensitive variables in local subflows.

claims.claim: The security article supplies patched earlier builds and says 2.67.143.26090 and later contain the fix.
claims.quote: If you need an update for an earlier release, get one of the following downloads: ... Release 2.67.143.26090 and all later versions include this security fix.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop flows do not need human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows are ideal for automating tasks that don't need human supervision.

claims.claim: CyberArk's certificate is opened and encrypted using the machine group's public key and is readable only from registered machines.
claims.quote: The certificate is opened and encrypted by using the public key of the machine group so it's only readable from the registered machines.

claims.claim: Desktop-flow connection credentials identify the account used to sign into the target machine.
claims.quote: Power Automate creates a new session for each unattended run on the machine using the credentials provided in the connection. The flow runs on this session, and then Power Automate signs it off.

claims.claim: The account's rights are a security boundary relevant to the exposure from its desktop flows.
claims.quote: Power Automate for desktop runs with the same user rights as the user who starts it.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/how-to/enable-ui-access for the account-rights premise; add that page to sources. The existing conditional advice to review privileged accounts need not change.

claims.claim: General Power Automate desktop-flow security controls cover credentials, sensitive variables, component access, DLP and auditing.
claims.quote: setting up credentials, managing sensitive variables, controlling access to desktop flows and related components, enforcing data loss prevention (DLP) policies, and capturing audit logs.

claims.claim: Sharing an Azure Key Vault credential also shares its environment variables.
claims.quote: By sharing your credential, all the environment variables used in the credential are shared as well.

claims.claim: Removing credential permissions does not remove permissions on the environment variables.
claims.quote: Removing permissions on a credential doesn't remove permissions on the environment variables.

claims.claim: primarycertificatefile carries the SSL client certificate encrypted with the group's public key.
claims.quote: Certificate that will be used as an SSL client certificate to contact the CCP. This field is encrypted with the group public key.

claims.claim: Credential use and sharing permissions are reached in Power Automate through Credentials > credential > Share.
claims.quote: go to Credentials. ... Select your credential from the list of credentials. ... On the command bar, select Share. ... Select Add people ... select the role you want to grant to this user
claims.fix: The path stops on the correct sharing pane. Extend controls[2].ui.path and its rendered table entry to 'Credentials > credential > Share > Add people > role' to reach the choice of use or sharing permissions, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/create-azurekeyvault-credential.

claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/GrantAccess grants a principal access to a credential record.
claims.quote: Grants a security principal (user, team, or organization) access to the specified record. ... Use the GrantAccess action with these entity types: ... Credential

claims.claim: GrantAccess's Target parameter identifies the credential record receiving the access grant.
claims.quote: Target ... The entity that is the target of the request to grant access.

claims.claim: PrincipalAccess identifies both the recipient and its access rights.
claims.quote: AccessMask ... The access rights of the security principal (user, team, or organization). ... Principal ... The security principal (user, team, or organization).
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/principalaccess to sources for the note's access-rights statement. Keep the GrantAccess docs link and existing note wording.

claims.claim: The correctly documented general credential-sharing control is not confirmed for Delinea-backed credentials.
claims.quote: Manage access through the dedicated page of each component in the Power Automate portal or through a Dataverse security role that grants access to the records in the component's table. ... Credentials | Use the Get credential action | Share a credential | Credential
claims.fix: Replace 'Existing credentials (Azure Key Vault page for the UI); not confirmed for Delinea-backed credentials.' in controls[2].note and its table entry with 'Applies to Credential records referenced by the Get credential action; manage their access through the component page or Dataverse security roles.' In the prose replace 'The other rows are existing controls for other credential stores or for credentials in general; Microsoft has not confirmed they govern Delinea-backed credentials.' with 'The CyberArk row is specific to CyberArk; the sharing row governs Credential records referenced by the Get credential action.' The cited Secure your data page states this general reach; a native Delinea creation contract remains undocumented.

claims.claim: CyberArk application information and its certificate can be configured per machine or machine group in the Power Automate portal.
claims.quote: To run a desktop flow on a machine or a group by using CyberArk credentials, add your CyberArk application information in the Power Automate portal. ... Select the certificate, which stores the private and the public key of the certificate.

claims.claim: The CyberArk guide says an application cannot currently be associated with machines or groups shared with other users.
claims.quote: You can't currently associate a CyberArk application with machines or groups that you share with other users.

claims.claim: The Dataverse credential table documents create, read, update and delete operations.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/credentials ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The credential table supports access-management operations.
claims.quote: The following operations can be used with the credential entity type. ... GrantAccess | Not Bound ... ModifyAccess | Not Bound ... RetrievePrincipalAccess | Not Bound ... RevokeAccess | Not Bound

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence or meter.
claims.quote: Power Automate will support Delinea Secret Server as an external credential provider for desktop flows. Organizations can securely use credentials managed in Delinea for machine sign-in and credential retrieval during attended and unattended automation.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The low cost rating and rationale classify known cost as staff time only despite the documented desktop-flow run meters.
claims.quote: cost: Low. The only cost the sources show for this feature is admin and security-team time ... attended desktop runs cost $0.60 per run unless the user's licence includes attended RPA, and unattended runs cost $3.00 per run
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. In pay-as-you-go environments, the preview Power Automate flow-run meters charge $0.60 per attended desktop run unless the user has attended RPA entitlement, and $3.00 per unattended run. No separate Delinea-provider meter or provider-specific licensing is published.' This uses the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters; the general meter covers desktop-flow runs and the absence of a provider-specific meter does not make known cost indirect-only.
